text:
tasha: Support forwarded a ticket: Rust quickstart fails for users who copy/paste into a new project. They get a compiler error about missing feature `async_closure` and an edition mismatch.

mike: which quickstart file? link?

tasha: quickstarts/rust/README.md. The snippet shows `tokio = \"0.2\"` in Cargo.toml and uses `async fn main` with `#[tokio::main]`, but the code also uses `async-clone` style macros and `async-trait` patterns that require newer tokio and edition 2021. New users copy only the src/main.rs block and forget Cargo.toml; others copy Cargo.toml but not the `[package] edition = \"2021\"` line. Results: "error: unstable feature" or "cannot find attribute macro `tokio` in this scope" depending on toolchain.

elaine: oh no. That's a classic snippet drift. The site copy button only copies the code block but not the Cargo.toml snippet we added elsewhere. New users run `cargo run` and wonder why it fails.

mike: short-term fix: update README to include a single copy/paste-safe section labeled "Minimal project (copy these three files)" with full Cargo.toml, src/main.rs, and a note about Rust toolchain >=1.62 and tokio >=1.16. Example Cargo.toml: 
```
[package]
name = \"redwood-quickstart\"
version = \"0.1.0\"
edition = \"2021\"

[dependencies]
redwood-inference = \"1\"
tokio = { version = \"1\", features = [\"macros\", \"rt-multi-thread\"] }
async-trait = \"0.1\"
```
And src/main.rs should show explicit imports and an example `#[tokio::main] async fn main()` rather than relying on unstable features.

tasha: also add `rust-toolchain` file content to pin toolchain in the example repo for reproducibility: `1.66.0` (or whatever minimum we pick). Some corporate CI uses older default toolchains.

elaine: UX nit: the copy button copies only the highlighted code block. Could we pair the Cargo.toml block with the main.rs block in a single combined block on the page (labeled \"copy all\")? If not, at least include a single combined block as Mike suggested so one copy covers everything.

mike: for the docs site we can add a combined block. Long-term: add a CI snippet that tries to build each language quickstart in a matrix of minimal supported versions to catch drift. docs-bot: can we auto-detect when code blocks for a sample are split across the page?

docs-bot: FYI: follow-up issue #6050 created to add quickstart CI builds. For this PR, tag docs/quickstart and sdk/rust and include minimum toolchain and tokio version. Also add a one-line about not copying partial examples.

support-bot: linked ticket #21009 from the user who hit the error; provided logs show both Rust 1.54 and tokio 0.2 in different repros. They attached the commands they ran.

tasha: I'm opening PR #6177: replaces fragmented snippets with a single "Minimal project" block, adds rust-toolchain content, updates Cargo.toml example to tokio 1.x and edition = \"2021\", and adds a small troubleshooting note for common build errors and how to `rustup override set` in CI.

mike: tiny wording suggestion: mention `cargo install rustup` is not idempotent in some CI images; prefer `rustup default` or using toolchain file. Also add a line about running `cargo build --release` for CI speed.

elaine: LGTM, left two minor comments on the PR about phrasing. :thumbsup:

mike: merging once CI passes. Also adding a follow-up to the docs PR template: include a checkbox "includes full copy/paste project (Cargo.toml + files) for language quickstarts".

tasha: thanks everyone. Hoping this cuts down on the support churn for Rust and avoids the painful rust edition surprises. :crab:
